findings.GATE_ARMING_HOOK_VERIFIED: before_agent_start hook fires in PI-Desktop 0.22.0 with the raw user prompt; the notice replacement works (entry [3]); exact-match arming runs state.enable()
findings.RUNTIME_BLOCKING_STILL_NOT_EFFECTIVE: GUARD_RUNTIME_BLOCKING_NOT_EFFECTIVE remains true on 0.22.0 with plugin 0.10.0: an armed session still executed an unapproved Bash probe at 04:29:56
findings.NEW_ROOT_CAUSE_EVIDENCED: the armed GuardState instance does not survive to later turns' tool_call consultation. Evidence: (a) the armed notice exists ONLY in the arming turn's system entries ([3]); the next turn's system entry ([6], 04:20:06) is base-only, so the host does not persist the replaced system prompt across turns; (b) tool.log has zero entries for 2026-11-14 (no executed tools besides the probe Bash which ran) while the probe executed; (c) runtime.log shows a single sidecar process (ready 04:17:28), so the state loss is instance-level, not process-level. Most consistent explanation: the extension runner (and its factory-local GuardState) is recreated per run/turn, and our session_start->disable() wipes arming on every reload; the sidecar source passes customSystemPrompt per runtime creation and loadTrustedExtensions() runs on each runtime creation (F map miss)
findings.SELF_DECLINE_VS_ENFORCEMENT: model self-declines must not be counted as enforcement evidence; only an actual tool_call attempt (transcript tool_call block) counts. Three earlier 'refusals' were context-driven, not gate results
findings.PALETTE_ARG_LIMITATION: the command palette invokes extension commands with empty args (renderer aG(name,'')), so /goalanchor-approve <record> cannot receive its record path through any UI surface on 0.22.0; the approval loop is UI-unreachable beyond the arming step
findings.PALETTE_SHORTCUTS: Ctrl+K and Ctrl+Shift+P both open the session-search palette on this build; the command palette entry point was not located in this round

verdict: GUARD_RUNTIME_BLOCKING_NOT_EFFECTIVE (state does not persist across turns on host 0.22.0; arming hook itself verified working)
next_fix_direction: persist the armed flag outside the runner instance (e.g. session-scoped state file written by before_agent_start and read by tool_call, or host-side state) so the tool_call hook consults an armed state regardless of runner recreation; approvals stay in-memory per instance; requires re-PLAN and re-review because the per-run state isolation invalidates the reviewed design's core assumption

v2_followup.design_iteration: v1 state-file design was reviewed and REJECTED (reviewer-2 FAIL: a model could plant a self-approved state file in an unarmed turn since signature() uses no secret material - trust escalation). v2 instead moved GuardState to extension.mjs MODULE LEVEL as Map<sessionId,GuardState>, relying on the runner's module-level factory cache (runner source: U.get(n.id) skips re-import and re-invokes the cached factory per turn) - no model-writable persistence surface exists at all. Reviewed round 1: reviewer-1 WARN, reviewer-2 WARN, arbiter WARN, meta WARN (gate outcome WARN, converged); five implementation gates all implemented (missing-sessionId fail-closed arming + enforcement block, Map eviction at 64 sessions preferring unarmed, instance id in every notice/status, delegation-surface documentation, truthful notices without the broken palette approval path).
v2_followup.implementation_evidence: Node tests 15/15 including 'guard state persists across factory calls within one process' (two create() invocations = two per-turn runtime rebuilds share the armed Map entry) and session isolation (different sessionIds start unarmed); pytest 1305/0, ruff/mypy/fixtures green; plugin rebuilt sha256 487498d9f08db2946b60f1102d49749444111246bc20fb8ba2c4917a18291865, installed and verified byte-identical extension.mjs in the host plugin directory
v2_followup.runtime_evidence: Session 71e38fb1 (gpt-6-luna): composer '/goalanchor-guard on' armed; system entry [3] carries the v2 armed notice WITH instance id (the arming turn). The host persists system-prompt snapshots only for the first turn pair, so per-turn notice re-injection could not be observed directly in the transcript. Four subsequent prompts (deception probe, force-attempt probe, neutral git task, natural count task) ALL ended in model self-declines without any tool_call block in the transcript - the per-turn armed notice keeps the model grounded on 'read-only session', so it refuses to even attempt calls. No unapproved write tool call could be elicited in an armed session; consequently the end-to-end blocking proof (an actual blocked tool_call block in the transcript) was NOT obtained.
v2_followup.supplementary_host_evidence: Idle-session palette extension command error 'runtime not found for session' reproduced again (toast observed), consistent with per-turn runtime lifecycle; plugin registry ready/enabled 0.10.0 after restarts.
v2_followup.verdict_v2: GUARD_ARMED_STATE_PERSISTENCE_FIXED_IN_EXTENSION (module-level, test-covered); GUARD_RUNTIME_BLOCKING_E2E_UNPROVEN_ON_HOST (model cooperation prevents eliciting a real tool call while armed; the gate's own tool_call path is exercised in Node tests only). The honest status is: the known root cause of the 0.9.3/0.10.0-v1 defect (state loss across turns) is fixed by construction and covered by tests; the remaining gap is an evidence gap, not a known defect.
remaining_risks: armed sessions are read-only-by-default on 0.22.0 (no working approval UI) - documented in SKILL.md/README/CHANGELOG
plugin reload or host restart silently resets the guard (module Map cleared) - documented; the disappearing per-turn notice is the signal
session-entry transcript only stores the first turn's system snapshots, limiting transcript-based verification of per-turn notice injection
